standard_prerequisites.name: An unramified ring map of finite type is locally standard etale, so after a principal localization there is an etale map onto the ring with a surjection from it
standard_prerequisites.use: Replaces the given map by a surjection from a standard etale algebra, which is the setting in which the injectivity argument is run.

standard_prerequisites.name: An etale algebra over a field is a finite product of fields, and an etale map is flat with the same minimal primes as the base, so the number of minimal primes is finite
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the fibre over the generic point and shows that the etale cover has finitely many minimal primes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Over a geometrically unibranch local ring the localization of an etale algebra at a prime is a domain, so the prime contains exactly one minimal prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the choice of an element that vanishes on all but one minimal prime so that the cover becomes a domain after localization.

core_obligations: Replace the map by a standard etale algebra with a surjection onto the given ring, keeping track of the preimage of the prime, and announce that the goal is to show that this surjection is injective after a principal localization (proof lines 31776-31779).

Reduce to the case where the etale cover is a domain: the cover is reduced because the base is a domain, its fibre over the generic point is a finite product of fields, its minimal primes lie over the generic point and are finitely many, and over the geometrically unibranch base the localization at the preimage of the prime is a domain, so exactly one minimal prime lies in that prime (proof lines 31781-31793).

Choose an element of the cover that does not lie in that one minimal prime but lies in all the others, and replace both rings by principal localizations at it so that the cover is a domain (proof lines 31793-31797).

Assume the cover is a domain, suppose the surjection is not injective, and let the nonzero kernel of the map on the localizations be considered; apply the previous lemma on ideals meeting the smaller domain to find a nonzero element of the localization of the base mapping to zero, contradicting the injectivity hypothesis (proof lines 31799-31814).
proof_roadmap: Pass to a standard etale cover with a surjection onto the given ring (proof lines 31776-31779).
Cut down to the case where the cover is a domain, using the finitely many minimal primes and the geometric unibranchness of the base (proof lines 31781-31797).
Conclude by contradiction through the previous lemma on ideals meeting the source domain (proof lines 31799-31814).
difficulty_reason: The statement assumes a domain as base, geometric unibranchness at the prime, unramifiedness of the map at the prime and injectivity of the localized map, and concludes that the map becomes etale after inverting one element outside the prime (statement lines 31762-31774). The proof first replaces the map by a standard etale cover with a surjection onto the given ring, then carries out a reduction to the case where that cover is a domain: it uses that the cover is reduced, that its fibre over the generic point is a finite product of fields so the minimal primes lie over the generic point, that a small number of them exist, and that geometric unibranchness makes the localization of an etale algebra at a prime a domain, after which an element separating the minimal primes produces the reduction (proof lines 31776-31797). The final step is a contradiction argument that invokes the previous lemma on ideals meeting the source domain, which is precisely why injectivity at the prime enters (proof lines 31799-31814). The counted span refers seven times, three times to results of this chapter and four times to other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
